elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained §13: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)... No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement." The redline deliberately preserves Vendor ownership, so Customer ownership of deliverables is not achieved.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; §13 expressly states no title passes to Sparkling.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §13 retained unchanged: Garman owns all intellectual property rights in the Work and related materials, logos and names.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The grant in §2 now reads "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free... licence", but the drafter's own analysis records that §17(a) limits the licence to the period while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated, and §17(a) is left unamended; the result is internally inconsistent. There is also no Customer-owned Deliverable to which embedded Vendor IP attaches.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: "irrevocable" in the amended §2 is contradicted by the untouched §17(a) termination-of-licence mechanic identified in the rationale.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Amended §2 grants a "royalty-free" licence and the additional-fee sentence ("subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule") has been deleted.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence only limits Garman's licence ("Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."); there is no affirmative statement that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in its data, including data converted under §4(b) and Schedule "D".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." No retained clause gives Garman broader exploitation rights over converted data.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists; §13 vests sole ownership of the Work in Garman and nothing creates shared title.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: §13 retained: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)..." — Vendor ownership of its platform/tools is preserved as the fallback permits.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: §2 now says "perpetual", but the drafter's rationale confirms §17(a) makes the licence last only while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated, and §17(a) was not edited. A retained sentence that extinguishes the licence on termination contradicts perpetuity, so the element is internally inconsistent rather than met.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "Irrevocable" in amended §2 is negated by the unamended §17(a) revocation-on-termination/non-payment mechanic identified in the finding rationale; no survival carve-out was added.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Amended §2 grants a "worldwide" licence and both the "operating at Authorized Locations" and "at each of the Authorized Locations" place-of-use caps and the additional-location fee sentence are deleted; the residual "at each AS400" is a platform, not a geographic, limit.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears in the grant and the sentence conditioning other-location use on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" has been struck.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Amended §2: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Sparkling's business purposes: (i) the Software, including any Improvements and Modifications... and (ii) the Documentation."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Sublicence right granted in §2 and the contradicting bar deleted from §3(c), which now reads "not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease or export the Work to any Person..." without the sublicence prohibition.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence expressly confines any Garman licence in Sparkling's data to processing "solely to provide the services under this Agreement", covering the Schedule "D" conversion activity in §4(b).

reasons: Fallback is incomplete on duration: "perpetual" and "irrevocable" are inserted in §2 but §17(a) — which the drafter's own rationale describes as ending the licence when fees stop or the Agreement terminates — is left untouched. Repair by amending §17(a) (or adding an express survival sentence in §2) to state that the licence granted in Section 2 survives expiry or termination of this Agreement and is not subject to Section 17(a), so the perpetual/irrevocable grant is not contradicted.

Preferred level fails on ownership/assignment (§13 keeps all title in Garman, no assignment to Sparkling) and on the absence of any affirmative "Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling's data" sentence; only a limitation on Garman's licence was added.

Intent is not preserved solely because of the retained §17(a) contradiction; all other retained mechanics (Authorized Locations definition still used in §4(b), AS400 platform wording, non-transferability, §13 ownership, assignment consent in §3(c)) survive coherently with no dangling references.

Minimality is satisfied: the edits are confined to what the fallback requires — deleting the place-of-use cap and additional-fee sentence (needed for worldwide/royalty-free), adding the perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free/use-modify-sublicense wording, extending the grant to Improvements and Modifications so it reaches the deliverables Sparkling funds under Schedule "D", removing only the directly contradicting sublicence bar in §3(c), and inserting one concise Customer Data processing-limitation sentence. No survival tails, damages, or unrelated boilerplate were added.
Once the §17(a) fix is made, the fallback checklist is complete and the finding can be closed at the fallback.
